title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC courtier similitude limps — condition vs goods
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: the similitude limps. Condition is faithfulness; goods are titles, dignities, estates—diverse and by nature separable. Those goods can be lost while faith is kept, or kept while faith is broken (war, dice, lawsuits, etc.). In Adam the 'goods' are rectitude, justice, holiness, and the condition is conserving those very goods. What Adam owed was perseverance in rectitude, justice, holiness, faith, duty—goods that already include faith and contain obedience to God.
pass_b_english: This similitude limps miserably. First, the condition is faithfulness; the goods are titles, dignities, estates. And so the condition, and the goods received under that condition, are things altogether diverse and by their nature separable. For those goods can be lost by war, or prodigality, or dice, or lawsuits rashly undertaken, or some other thing, while faith is kept—or, faith being violated, can be retained. Here, however, the goods are rectitude, justice, holiness; the condition is the conservation of these very goods. For what was required of Adam except that he persevere in rectitude, justice, holiness, faith, duty? Do not these very goods include faith? do they not contain obedience to God?
source_text: Haec similitudo misere claudicat. Primum conditio est fidelitas; bona tituli, dignitates, fundi. Itaque conditio, & bona sub illa conditione accepta sunt res admodum diversae, & natura sua separabiles. Possunt enim bona illa bello, vel profusione, vel alea, vel litibus temere susceptis, vel aliqua alia re amitti conservata fide, aut hac violata retineri. Hic vero bona sunt rectitudo, justitia, sanctitas, conditio horum ipsorum bonorum conservatio. Quid enim ab Adamo exigebatur nisi ut perseveraret in rectitudine, justitia, sanctitate, fide, officio? Annon haec ipsa bona fidem includunt? obedientiam Deo continent.

choices.choice: Condition vs goods separable in courtier, not in Adam's moral goods
